title: Getting started
desc: Install from Steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout.
text: 01 — first launch install & first run ikandy is a windows desktop app, installed through steam. no account beyond steam, no setup wizard: you can be visualizing system audio in under a minute. install open ikandy on steam and install it like any other steam app. launch it from your steam library. steam keeps it updated automatically. on first launch ikandy indexes the preset library and runs a background reactivity scan. this takes a few seconds and happens silently while you use the app. a short welcome walks you in, a one-time photosensitivity notice shows before anything flashes, and the ? on the console replays the guided tour whenever you want it. what it needs windows 10 or 11 and any reasonably modern gpu. ikandy performs fully offline: no account, no sign-in, and nothing about your show depends on the internet. online, the app talks to our servers only for housekeeping like the current ai price sheet and, if enabled, anonymous diagnostics and usage stats - never your music, files, or identity. fastest path to visuals start playing music in any app on your computer, then in ikandy pick now playing as the source. no setup, no auth — ikandy listens to whatever windows is currently playing and starts reacting immediately. the layout one screen, one console ikandy has one layout: the full screen is the stage, and a slim console bar lives at the bottom. everything routes through that bar. when you step up to performing, stage is a second surface built for the job, and the main window always shows a return button when stage has control. the console bar, left to right now playing : album art, track title, artist. click the art to open synced lyrics. the source pill under the title shows what is connected; click it to change sources. playback : play, pause, skip, volume, and a seek bar. works with spotify, foobar2000, vlc, and system audio. engine + presets : tabs pick the engine that is driving the stage: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , or image . arrows step through looks, browse opens the full library, and auto cycles on a dwell timer you set. vibe + output : the vibe popover shapes bloom, motion blur, and post intensity. the scenes popover switches hand-built scenes with a per-scene intensity control. the master audio popover sets how much bass, mid, and treble drive the visuals, with a mix control, a master intensity fader, and a god-rays toggle. output opens the logo overlay , and the lut control can auto-pick a color grade per scene or cycle grades per preset. view + settings : fullscreen, hide the console, the black or chrome theme, a knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, multi-monitor output, and the gear for sources & settings. the ? replays the guided tour any time. popovers, not buried menus deep controls live in small popovers that open from the bar: vibe, scenes, master audio, and luts. the gear opens the one real modal, sources & settings , for connecting sour welcome tour photosensitivity seizure notice

title: Audio sources + controls
desc: Now Playing, Spotify, per-app capture with Smart Auto, bass/mid/treble drive, shuffle, playlists.
text: 03 — audio sources connect your music ikandy can connect to four different sources. each one offers a different feature set depending on what its underlying api exposes. switching between them automatically pauses the previous one. 🎵 spotify ● full features · premium recommended the richest integration. track info, album art, synced lyrics, playlist browser with search, and full transport — play, pause, skip, shuffle modes including smart shuffle detection. ikandy uses bring your own key auth: you create a free spotify developer app and paste the client id once. it’s saved encrypted via windows dpapi and never leaves your machine. one-time setup in ikandy, click the source pill on the console (or open ⚙ → source ) and choose spotify . the settings panel shows the exact redirect uri to register. go to developer.spotify.com/dashboard , log in, and click create app . give it any name and description. under redirect uris , paste the uri shown in ikandy. check the web api box. save. open the new app → settings → copy the client id . paste the client id into ikandy's spotify settings and click connect . spotify opens in your browser to authorise. done. ikandy's spotify settings panel showing the client id field and redirect uri why byok most apps embed a shared client id, so spotify rate-limits everyone using that app together. with byok, your ikandy uses your own quota — no sharing, no throttling. premium required for transport spotify's web api only allows playback control for premium subscribers. free accounts get track info, album art, and lyrics, but playback buttons are greyed out. works with spotify desktop, the web player, or any spotify connect device. 🎧 foobar2000 ● full features · beefweb plugin for the audiophile crowd. connects via the foo_beefweb component — a rest/json api that exposes the full library. playlist browse with search, every shuffle mode foobar supports, transport, album art, lyrics. the most feature-complete source ikandy offers. one-time setup download and install foo_beefweb from github.com/hyperblast/beefweb/releases . in foobar2000: file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control . tick enable http server (default port 8880 ). optionally set a password. click apply. in ikandy, choose foobar2000 , leave port at 8880 , enter the password if set, and click connect . foobar2000 → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control 📺 vlc ● standard · local http connects to vlc’s built-in web interface — play, pause, skip, shuffle on/off, album art, synced lyrics. no library browse; pick what to play in vlc, control playback in ikandy. one-time setup open vlc → tools → preferences . switch show settings to all . navigate to interface → main interfaces and tick web . expand main inte source tab connect disconnect reconnect greyed smtc drag file

title: Visualizers + presets
desc: Five engines on one stage. MilkDrop, cycling, reactivity, your own presets.
text: visualizers five engines, one stage the engine tabs on the console pick what is driving the stage: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , or image . milkdrop is the deep preset library this page covers; glsl and webgpu run hand-built and imported scenes , spout turns a live feed into a source, and image layers fx shaders over a photo. milkdrop, reborn the milkdrop engine is built on butterchurn, a webgl port of the legendary milkdrop visualizer. ikandy ships a deep preset library: the base collection, extra curated packs, and an image category that layers especially well over a background photo. cycling looks auto on the console cycles presets on a dwell timer you set: how many seconds each look holds before the next. the sliders icon next to it opens timing and blend controls; a longer blend morphs cinematically between looks, a short one cuts kinetic. auto-cycle draws from a shuffle bag, so every preset in the active pool plays once before any can repeat. reactivity on first launch ikandy quietly scores the library in the background while you use the app, classifying each preset as reactive, non-reactive, or image-texture. the results are cached. in the browser, the reactive filter narrows the pool to presets that visibly answer the music; if the scan has not finished, a run scan button is right there. there is also a reactivity master for the whole engine: turn it down and presets settle into calm ambient motion instead of going dark, turn it up and the beat drives harder. the browser browse opens the full library with thumbnails. hover any card for a live preview; click to load it on the stage immediately. scene cards preview from a cached clip the same way. tabs, favorites, hiding, flagging, and reordering are covered in library . your own presets in the browser, custom presets loads a folder of converted butterchurn json presets , merged alongside the bundled library and remembered across restarts. butterchurn uses a json preset format rather than milkdrop's original .milk binaries; if a folder contains .milk files, ikandy says so and points you at the converter. misbehaving presets some presets produce invalid values on modern gpus. ikandy skips broken or near-black presets automatically and remembers them, so the cycle keeps moving. anything questionable lands in the flagged tab for you to judge.  engines glsl webgpu spout image butterchurn json milk converter shuffle bag reactive scan custom folder

title: Library: browse + manage
desc: Nine tabs, search, maker pills, favorites, My Scenes, previews, saving, file types.
text: one browser, nine tabs every visual in ikandy lives in one browser. the top tabs split it by kind, each with its own identity color: milkdrop , glsl , webgpu , spout , and images for your picture library, then my scenes for the things you have made, and the three curation tabs: favorites , hidden , flagged . find it fast search filters the grid as you type, with a one-tap clear. category tabs inside milkdrop narrow the pool: all, reactive (from the reactivity scan ), your custom presets, and more. maker pills filter milkdrop by preset author with one click; glsl and webgpu get the same artist pills for their scenes. random pulls one look from the current pool and drops you straight back on the stage. three densities : list, grid, and large. large keeps cards big enough to actually read. curate it star anything : every card carries a favorite star, the favorites tab and its count update live, and shuffle can be told to draw from favorites only. hide what you never want in rotation; flag what needs a second look. both get their own tabs, so nothing is ever lost. drag to reorder : every grid in the browser reorders by drag, and your order sticks. previews hover any milkdrop card and it live-renders in a preview popup. scene cards on the visual, webgpu, and spout tabs play a cached clip on hover instead, so previews stay instant. click any card to put it on the stage immediately. my scenes scenes you compose or generate land in my scenes. each card can be replayed, renamed, or deleted. imported presets start as pending; promote the keepers into your own custom category with one action. saving, editing, versions from the studio, save as new creates a fresh asset and overwrite updates the one you are editing. originals and templates are protected: they can only be saved as new, never overwritten, and a duplicate-name guard keeps two assets from colliding. file types the image library accepts png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, and svg, and feeds both backgrounds and the logo maker . shaders paste in as glsl or wgsl text, milkdrop presets load as converted butterchurn json (the app detects .milk files and points you at the converter), and ai scenes travel as .vis packages with their provenance intact. browse music and visuals together the sync button opens the preset browser and the playlist panel as a pair, so you can line up the next track and the next look side by side.  spout images tab search maker pills author random list grid large density star sync playlist

title: Scenes
desc: The hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets.
text: custom scenes audio-reactive, built in-house scenes are direct audio-reactive engines written for ikandy, driven by real-time frequency analysis. where a milkdrop preset interprets a recipe of math, a scene is code that listens: the music literally makes the picture. a library across four runtimes the scene library has grown far past its first handful, and it spans four runtimes: glsl fragment scenes, canvas2d scenes, three.js scenes, and webgpu compute scenes when your gpu supports them. the range runs from classic spectrum work (flames, bars, sweeping rays) to deep-space flythroughs, gravitational lenses, particle trails, and heavy compute pieces. flight scenes even take a game controller: plug one in and fly . turning scenes on open the scenes popover from the console and pick a card; it plays immediately. every scene has an intensity control for how hard it answers the audio, and scenes that need more expose their own row of controls right there: tone knobs, a god-rays switch, a color-grade slot. the house rule audio drives light and color, never the camera. nothing on screen shakes to the beat; when a scene has a camera, it belongs to you or the autopilot. it is why ikandy stays watchable for hours. layering scenes sit over the milkdrop stage and over fx images. drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover to let a scene take center stage, or keep it high and blend the two. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. make your own scenes you compose, import, or generate with ai land in my scenes , ready to replay, rename, or put in a rundown.  three.js canvas2d webgpu compute flight intensity god rays lut

title: FX shaders
desc: Real-time post effects and the FX image pipeline.
text: fx real-time fx shaders fx is three layers deep in ikandy: living treatments over an image, a post chain over everything, and a play layer for your hands. fx images pick a background photo on the image engine and run a live treatment over it. the set covers weather and texture (rain, fog, heat haze, dust film), analog and broadcast decay (vhs warp, data corruption, hologram), and paint and material (ink bleed, watercolor, liquid metal, shatter, plasma arc). every treatment is audio-aware, and the library keeps growing. the post chain a multi-pass post chain runs over the whole show: bloom, chromatic aberration, grain, scanlines, vignette, and contrast, each on a live knob with its own status light, plus tone and lut color grading and a god-rays pass. beat-reactive particle bursts ride on top as their own layer. this is the finish that makes everything underneath read like one image. the play layer mouse fx and draw mode put the pointer in the show: click ripples, freehand drawing with adjustable width, and particle trails, all blended over the visuals without ever touching the camera. performance quality tiers (battery, standard, high, ultra) scale the render resolution and supersampling, so the same show runs right on a laptop on battery and on a desktop pushing a wall.  rain fog vhs hologram ink watercolor liquid metal bloom chromatic aberration scanlines vignette contrast particle burst draw ripple quality tier battery ultra

title: Spout in + out
desc: Publish visuals to OBS and VJ software, or post-process any incoming feed.
text: spout a node in the rig spout is gpu texture sharing between windows apps: no capture cards, no encoding, no added latency worth naming. ikandy speaks it in both directions. spout out: publish the show turn on spout output in sources & settings, give the sender a name, and ikandy appears as a source in obs, resolume, touchdesigner, madmapper, vmix, and anything else that receives spout. what gets published is the show itself: the composited visuals, never the console or any ui chrome. toasts and panels stay off the feed by design. the output is occlusion-immune: it keeps rendering at full pace even when the ikandy window is covered or minimized, so you can work in other apps while the feed runs. the audio path is never touched. overlays on the broadcast two switches decide what rides on everything you broadcast, the second screen and spout and recordings alike: the now playing card and lyrics . one switch per overlay, so a clean feed is one click away. spout in: post-process anything pipe a live feed into ikandy from obs, touchdesigner, resolume, or madmapper: pick the sender in source → spout in (any active sender shows up, with a refresh), choose a frame rate up to 60, and the feed becomes a source. the browser's spout tab holds the scenes built to treat a live feed, so someone else's video comes out wearing ikandy's light. tier note spout output ships in the stage tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative.  sender name obs resolume touchdesigner madmapper vmix occlusion broadcast overlay now playing lyrics clean feed

title: Wallpaper + displays
desc: Any visual behind your icons. Mirror or Span, per display, survives Explorer restarts.
text: set the desktop as your stage live wallpaper runs the visual behind your desktop icons while you work, on any mix of displays, driven by whatever ikandy is listening to. it is a set-and-forget output: open sources & settings → live wallpaper , click a display to toggle it on, and get back to work. change the visual any time from the console or stage and the desktop follows. the wallpaper survives explorer restarts, and it keeps rendering even when the main ikandy window is covered or minimized. fit mode: mirror or span mirror (the default) puts the same feed on each screen you picked. span stretches one image across all attached displays as a single canvas; it needs two or more screens, and it takes over the routing while it is on. both modes persist. the output window separate from wallpaper, the multi-display output window is a broadcast surface: mirror the main view onto the displays you choose, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous visual edge to edge (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). right-click the fullscreen button for a quick "send to a second screen" chooser. add hide-ui mode and the pixels are all that is left. overlays the now playing card and lyrics each have a broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings, or keep every output clean. good to know toggle wallpaper off any time from the same panel if anything misbehaves. performance cost scales with the visual you pick. calm scenes cost very little; heavy compute scenes cost more. tier note desktop wallpaper ships in the pro tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative.  mirror span fit mode explorer restart output window gain hide ui send second screen overlays

title: Lyrics
desc: Synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none.
text: lyrics words on the show synced lyrics ride the visuals, line by line, timed to the track. click the album art on the console to open them; click again to put them away. three modes classic draws the current line clean over the show. physics hands each line to a physics simulation, so words drift, swing, and settle with their own weight. native uses the source's own lyric display where one exists. make them yours position the line at the top, center, or bottom of the stage, scale the font from subtle to headline, set the opacity, and pick a color: the theme accent, white, or a swatch of your own. where the words come from sources that carry synced lyrics, like spotify, supply their own. everything else falls back to the community lrclib database. very new or obscure tracks may have no entry, which is where the next part comes in. add your own: tap to time open add lyrics and paste the words. if they already carry timestamps, they play immediately. if they are plain text, tap to time turns timing them into a performance: play the track and stamp each line the moment it lands. seekable sources get a small timeline with previous, play, and next, so a missed stamp is a two-second fix, not a restart. saved lyrics live in your local lyrics folder, keyed by title and artist, and you can point ikandy at a folder of your own. on the broadcast lyrics have their own broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings , or keep the output clean. tier note physics lyrics and the tap-to-time editor ship in the pro tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative.  classic physics native mode tap to time timestamp add lyrics folder lrclib position size color broadcast

title: STAGE: perform
desc: Now/Next decks, GO with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos.
text: the console you perform from stage is the live view: a broadcast desk for planning a night and steering it in real time. when stage is live, the main window shows a return button so you always know which surface has control. now, next, go two decks with live previews: now is what the room sees, next is what you have lined up. click next to pick a look from the library, long-press to grab whatever is currently playing, right-click to clear. hit go and next takes the stage with a real crossfade: the outgoing frame freezes and dissolves into the incoming look, so transitions read as intentional, never as a cut. hold pins the current look against the autopilot. ride the moment a row of momentary performance keys sits under your fingers: blackout , a beat-locked strobe (hard photosensitive-safety cap of three flashes per second), and freeze . press and hold; release and the show returns. every stage control carries an address, so all of it lands on midi and osc . pads hot-cue pads hold looks you want on a trigger, each with a live thumbnail. assign a pad, hit it when the room needs it. rundowns, plans, pools, autopilot build a rundown for the night: concrete entries play a specific look with its own duration, pool entries shuffle from a group you curated. reorder by drag; unset entries flag themselves so nothing surprises you mid-set. autopilot follows the rundown, or smart-shuffles when none is loaded, with a dwell you pick from seconds to minutes and a live countdown to the next switch. shows new / save / load / delete manage whole shows: a saved show carries the rundown, your pads, and the per-output setup, so friday's rig comes back with one load. combos the combos tab is a layer compositor with a live preview: stack looks into a composite, save it, and recall the whole stack in one click. tempo and the logo tap four or more times to set the bpm by feel; double-click to clear it. the logo button opens the image studio to build or edit your overlay and lights up whenever one is live. outputs route per screen, so the projector and the stream can carry different dressing. stage ships in the stage tier. tier contents at launch are listed on the pricing page ; the steam page is authoritative.  now next go crossfade hold blackout strobe freeze pads hot cue rundown show save load combos compositor dwell countdown per output routing

title: Logo maker
desc: Image Studio: text or image, chrome and matte finishes, live on any visual.
text: image studio: make the logo the logo maker builds a broadcast-style overlay that rides on top of any running visual: your name, your mark, live on the output. create start from text or bring an image from your library. a studio preview backdrop helps you judge it, and it is preview only: your logo stays transparent and the backdrop is never baked into the asset. finishes two live material finishes ship today: chrome , liquid metal that catches the scene, and black , a matte powder-coat. each asset also carries its own audio-reactivity control, so the logo can breathe with the music or hold still. save and apply apply live puts it on the output immediately. save as new keeps a version; originals and templates are protected from overwrite. on stage, the logo button opens the studio directly and lights up whenever an overlay is live, so you always know it is on.  logo image studio overlay chrome matte black brand watermark apply live save

title: MIDI, phone remote, gamepad
desc: Bind hardware with MIDI Learn, steer from your phone over LAN, fly with a controller.
text: hands on the rig three ways to drive ikandy without touching the mouse: hardware midi, your phone, and a game controller. midi learn click midi learn , then move a control on your hardware. that knob or fader is now bound. bindings can be exported and imported as json, so a rig setup travels with you. phone remote (lan) start the phone remote and any phone on your local network can steer the show from its browser. no app to install, nothing leaves your lan. for locked-down networks there is a source-ip allowlist: list the devices allowed to send, or leave it empty to accept all local senders. gamepad flight flight scenes accept a controller with zero setup: plug one in and any input takes the controls. left stick steers, right stick looks, right trigger throttle, left trigger brake. hands off for five seconds and the autopilot resumes; tab or the b button hands back instantly. the mouse never touches the camera, it belongs to the ui. midi and osc control ship in the stage tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative.  midi learn osc phone remote lan gamepad controller flight bindings osc receiver port address lighting desk show controller tick green

title: AI scene generation
desc: Bring your own key. Generate, fix, and tune scenes at provider cost.
text: an ai that writes scenes, at cost ikandy can generate new visual scenes with ai, and can repair or tune imported shaders in the ai shader studio. it is bring-your-own-key: you paste a key from your ai provider and pay them directly. ikandy adds no markup and sells no credits. your key stays yours the key is encrypted with the operating system's secure storage the moment you paste it. the app's rendering layer never sees the raw key, and it never leaves your machine except to talk to your provider. what it can do generate : describe a look and get a runnable scene. ai fix : paste a shader that will not compile and let the sandbox repair it. the sandbox is designed to catch errors safely so they don't take the app down. ai tune : ask for adjustments to a working scene, in plain language. costs because you pay the provider directly, costs are the provider's list prices. typical fixes and tunes cost cents. ikandy shows a live cost estimate before you run a job, using current provider pricing. guided ai scene generation ships in the pro tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative.  ai generate byok key anthropic fix tune shader import studio cost

title: Controls, themes, tips
desc: Reactivity, seek and volume, three theme layers, UI size, workflow tips.
text: controls & themes tune the whole thing the console is the control surface; this page is the small print around it. reactivity, everywhere it matters every engine carries a reactivity control: turn it down and the visuals settle into calm ambient motion, turn it up and they snap to the beat. the master audio popover goes further with bass, mid, and treble drive , a mix control, and the master intensity fader. sensible defaults sit in the middle and work for most music. the seek bar the progress bar in the playback zone is draggable: click and drag anywhere on it to seek, on every source that supports seeking. volume lives right next to it for sources that allow control; anything that does not is greyed with a hint, not hidden. three layers of theme console material : black , a matte powder-coat, or chrome , liquid metal with dark text. the whole board, browser, and playlist panel change together. accent color : swatches like gold, neon, forest, ember, lavender, and crimson, plus a custom picker and a random that surprises you. the accent runs through every knob, tab, and led. panel background : schemes including slate and the light cloud, plus a panel opacity slider so the chrome can float over the show as much or as little as you like. add the knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, and a ui size setting for readability at couch distance. themes change the chrome, never the visuals. set it once, forget it everything persists across sessions: reactivity, theme, accent, source preferences, custom preset folders, the last-used look. close it, reopen it, it is your rig. workflow tips spotlight a scene or image : drop the milkdrop opacity in its settings popover to 30 to 50 percent and let the layer underneath breathe through. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. for recording or streaming : classic lyric mode over a clean scene with a subtle analog fx reads beautifully on video, and the broadcast overlay switches keep the feed intentional. lyrics need honest metadata : correct artist and title fetch the right words. if lyrics look wrong, check the tags on the playing source first.  black chrome theme accent gold neon forest ember lavender crimson slate cloud panel opacity ui size knobs sliders seek volume persist

title: Troubleshooting + help
desc: Fixes for the common snags, and where to reach a human.
text: 10 — troubleshooting when things get weird the most common issues people run into, and how to fix them. click any item to expand. now playing says "nothing is playing" windows reports no app is currently registered as the smtc owner. simply start playing music in any app and the message will disappear within a second. if music is playing and now playing still doesn’t see it: firefox — open about:config , set media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled to true , restart firefox. chrome / edge — check chrome://flags for hardware media key handling and set it to enabled . apple music for windows — can be inconsistent. try pausing/resuming, or use a dedicated source instead. now playing controls grey out / next or previous don't work by design. ikandy queries the active app for which transport commands it actually exposes — some apps (single youtube videos, podcasts) don’t advertise next or previous, so ikandy locks those buttons. hover any greyed-out button to see the reason. for full transport, use a youtube mix or playlist url, or spotify desktop/web player. "could not start audio source" / no audio reactivity windows treats system audio capture the same as microphone access for privacy purposes. fix: settings → privacy & security → microphone → toggle let desktop apps access your microphone on. restart ikandy. if that doesn’t help, click 🎤 reconnect audio in settings (⚙) → source tab . spotify playback controls are greyed out spotify only allows external playback control for premium subscribers — this is a spotify api restriction. free accounts still get track info, album art, and synced lyrics. premium users: the dedicated source works whether you’re playing in spotify desktop, web player, mobile, or a spotify connect speaker. spotify won't connect / authentication fails most common cause: the redirect uri in your spotify developer app doesn't exactly match the one ikandy shows. open ikandy's spotify settings, copy the redirect uri, then go to developer.spotify.com/dashboard → your app → settings → paste it into redirect uris . save, then retry connect from ikandy. also check: client id pasted with no leading/trailing spaces, web api box is ticked. vlc won't connect open http://localhost:8080 in a browser — you should see the vlc web ui password prompt. if you don't, the web interface isn't enabled. fix: vlc → tools → preferences → show settings: all → interface → main interfaces → tick web . expand lua below it and confirm a lua http password is set. restart vlc. foobar2000 won't connect in foobar2000 → file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control , confirm enable http server is ticked. test by visiting http://localhost:8880 in a browser. if you see the beefweb player, the plugin is healthy. if you set a pa discord report bug email support reactivity quality tier
